items.title: How AI plotted an interstellar journey to Alpha Centauri
items.excerpt: The Fermi Explorer Mission plans to launch a spacecraft toward our nearest star by the end of 2029, using a gravity-assist trajectory discovered by an AI search rather than by human mission planners.
items.rationale: An AI search found a gravity-assist route human mission planners missed — the first time a machine-designed trajectory anchors a real interstellar launch date.

items.title: New AI model maps the ion binding sites that control how proteins work
items.excerpt: Constructor University and Constructor Labs built BiteNetI, a deep-learning model that locates binding sites for 14 biologically important ion types directly in 3D protein structures in seconds, reporting two- to threefold higher accuracy than most existing predictors including DeepMind's AlphaFold 3.
items.rationale: Ion sites decide whether a protein actually works; a seconds-fast model claiming 2-3x the accuracy of AlphaFold 3 on them is an immediately usable structural-biology tool.

items.title: IBM quantum computer solves classically intractable problem in 15 minutes
items.excerpt: IBM and University of Chicago researchers completed a quantum computation that leading classical methods could not practically reproduce, using 70 error-corrected logical qubits and finishing in roughly 15 minutes with statistical evidence the result was reliable.
items.rationale: 70 error-corrected logical qubits finishing in 15 minutes, with a reliability argument attached, moves the quantum-advantage debate from claim to measurable baseline.

items.title: Mapping global methane emissions from space with deep learning
items.excerpt: Google Research describes a deep-learning pipeline that turns satellite spectra into global methane emission maps, detecting plumes and attributing them to sources at planetary scale.
items.rationale: Turning raw satellite spectra into attributed methane plumes at planetary scale gives climate researchers a source-level monitoring layer that did not exist before.

items.title: New AI uses a fresh approach to reasoning that's potentially much cheaper
items.excerpt: Researchers say a new reasoning architecture costs up to 11 times less to run than a leading OpenAI model while matching it on benchmark tasks, a shift with direct consequences for compute-bound research labs.
items.rationale: Reasoning in latent space instead of chains of words cuts inference cost up to 11x at matched benchmark scores — the compute math for research labs changes overnight.
